categories.main_business_segments: Under Armour operates primarily in four geographic segments: North America, EMEA (Europe, Middle East, and Africa), Asia-Pacific, and Latin America. The company’s principal business activities are the development, marketing, and distribution of branded performance apparel, footwear, and accessories for men, women, and youth. Apparel is the largest segment by revenue, followed by footwear and accessories. The company also generates a small portion of revenue from licensing arrangements.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Under Armour’s products are engineered with proprietary performance technologies such as HEATGEAR®, COLDGEAR®, HOVR®, UA Flow™, and UA RUSH™. The company focuses on technical fabrications and advanced materials to enhance athletic performance, comfort, and fit. Manufacturing is outsourced to unaffiliated contract manufacturers, with raw materials sourced from a limited number of pre-approved suppliers, primarily in Asia. Product development emphasizes innovation in materials, fit, and performance features.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company serves a broad customer base including athletes at all levels, sports teams, and consumers with active lifestyles. Key markets include national and regional sporting goods chains, independent and specialty retailers, department stores, institutional athletic departments, and leagues, as well as direct-to-consumer shoppers through owned stores and e-commerce. No single customer accounts for more than 10% of net revenues, and the company targets both performance-driven and casual-use consumers.
categories.geographic_coverage: Under Armour has a global footprint, with North America (primarily the United States and Canada) accounting for about 60% of net revenues. EMEA, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America collectively represent the remaining 40%. The company operates retail stores and e-commerce platforms in key international markets and distributes products through third-party logistics providers and independent distributors in regions where it lacks direct operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: Under Armour is positioned as a downstream brand owner and marketer, focusing on product design, development, and distribution. The company outsources manufacturing to third-party contract manufacturers and sources raw materials from pre-approved suppliers. It manages inventory, marketing, and sales, but does not own or operate manufacturing facilities, placing it at the downstream end of the apparel and footwear supply chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include driving premium brand growth, expanding direct-to-consumer and digital channels, and enhancing operational efficiency through restructuring. The company invests in product innovation, sustainable materials, and digital engagement to strengthen brand connectivity. R&D efforts focus on developing new performance technologies, improving fit and comfort, and integrating sustainability into product design and operations.
categories.revenue_model: Under Armour generates revenue primarily through the sale of branded apparel, footwear, and accessories via wholesale and direct-to-consumer channels, including owned retail stores and e-commerce. Wholesale accounts for 58% of net revenues, direct-to-consumer for 40%, and licensing for 2%. The company also earns revenue from licensing its trademarks to third parties for select product categories.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include Nike, adidas, PUMA, and lululemon athletica, all of which have strong global brand recognition and, in some cases, greater resources. Under Armour differentiates itself through a focus on athletic performance and technical innovation but faces intense competition from both global and regional brands, as well as private label offerings from retailers. The company is positioned as a premium performance brand but has experienced recent market share and revenue declines.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, Under Armour reported net revenues of $5.16 billion, a 9.4% decrease from the prior year. The company posted a net loss of $201 million, reflecting restructuring charges, litigation expenses, and declining sales, particularly in North America and Asia-Pacific. Gross margin improved to 47.9%, but overall the company is experiencing a challenging growth environment with a focus on operational restructuring and profitability improvement.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Under Armour emphasizes making athletes better through innovative, performance-driven products that offer superior comfort, fit, and technical benefits compared to non-performance alternatives. The brand is built on authenticity, with strong ties to athletes and teams, and leverages proprietary technologies to differentiate its apparel and footwear. The company also highlights sustainability and digital engagement as emerging elements of its value proposition.
